clue.text: Housework will be split to show enterprise

definitions.text: Housework will be split to show enterprise

parts.words: Housework will be split to show enterprise
parts.note: split the word housework into house and work, then swap each half for a grander synonym: a small dwelling and diligent labour, together naming a kind of business

explanation.surface: A warning that chores will be shared out to demonstrate initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: A small country house is a cottage and work is industry; together they name small-scale manufacturing done at home, the 'enterprise' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is the term for a small business carried on in workers' own homes, a form of enterprise.

clue.text: Soup for an American cowherd needs stirring

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of the herdsman word are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cattle hand on the range has a pot of something to stir.
explanation.definitionFit: This thick seafood or corn soup is a classic dish of the United States, especially New England.

clue.text: What ancients wore to speak at length?

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly and at length

explanation.surface: A question about what old-timers wore when giving long speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose robes were the outer garments of citizens in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Blast area for sculpting stone

indicators.note: sculpting shapes material into a new form, so the letters are reshaped into a different order

explanation.surface: A quarry blast zone set aside for getting carving stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine white translucent mineral, a type of stone prized by sculptors.

clue.text: Target on river in Yorkshire is bear

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal, a target
the Ure is a river flowing through North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An aim on a Yorkshire river turns out to be a large animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb: to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to tolerate it, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Try to impress — call doctor before work

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone eager to impress phones a doctor before getting down to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentioning famous acquaintances casually is a way of trying to impress listeners.

clue.text: This fruit bug lives to a limited extent

indicators.note: to a limited extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An insect makes its home in a piece of fruit, though only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican citrus hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine, a fruit known for its wrinkled skin.

clue.text: Detours planned to include gold heraldic emblem

indicators.note: to include means one piece is placed within the other
a planned route is arranged afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Diversions are mapped out around a golden badge.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold, apt beside 'heraldic emblem'; the clue's own word 'Detours' supplies the rest once rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-and-white flower badge of the Tudor dynasty is a famous emblem in English heraldry.

clue.text: Chinese money protecting tiger maybe in part of Mexico

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the yuan is the currency unit of China
a tiger is one example of a big cat

explanation.surface: Chinese funds being spent to protect a big cat in a Mexican region.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yucatán is a peninsula and state in south-east Mexico, a region of the country.

clue.text: Doing sentry duty in rocky ground screening west of airport

indicators.note: screening means hiding something behind or within, so one piece goes inside the other
rocky means unsteady or shaken up, so the letters are jumbled
in an across entry west is the left-hand end, so this takes the first letter

explanation.surface: A guard stands on stony ground hiding from the western side of an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' turns GROUND into ONGURD; 'screening' places A, from 'west of airport', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is watchful and alert, which is what the phrase means: ready for danger.

clue.text: Pleasant-sounding doctor takes look inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a medic is a doctor
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A physician pleasant to listen to takes a peek inside a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tuneful is pleasant to the ear, the musical sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Gave up hope, seeing legal document cut by second couple

indicators.note: cut by says the document is split open with something placed inside

parts.note: a deed is a legal document such as a conveyance
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Someone loses heart on seeing a legal agreement altered by another pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose all hope is the meaning of this verb, a direct synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Very dry beast with no tail

indicators.note: with no tail means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a brute is a beast or animal

explanation.surface: A tailless animal described as extremely dry, like a dull joke.
explanation.definitionFit: On champagne labels this term marks the driest style, with very little sugar added.

clue.text: Italian bridge books returned by rail, mistakenly

indicators.note: mistakenly suggests the letters are written wrongly, so they are rearranged
returned means the books abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Library books on an Italian bridge are sent back by train in error.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous old bridge over the Grand Canal in Venice, Italy.

clue.text: Worker getting one over one, for starters

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
I is the Roman numeral for one
past means over or finished
I again is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An employee taking one thing after another, to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' looks like an instruction to take first letters; here 'starters' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian appetisers served before the main meal are starters, the plural noun matching.

clue.text: Record including name and instrument used for such cattle

indicators.note: including says one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a log is a written record
a horn is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: A log that names an instrument used for herding cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of cattle with very long horns, so the word names such animals, singular or plural.

clue.text: Bizarre request — go in confusion

indicators.note: letters in confusion are jumbled, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd demand to leave, made in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grotesque is strangely distorted or absurd, a close synonym of weird.

clue.text: Son heads on holiday and calls on the way

parts.note: s is the genealogical abbreviation for son
the heads of things are their tops
a person off work is on holiday

explanation.surface: A son leads others on holiday and visits places along the route.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause a journey somewhere briefly is to break the trip, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Most of planet consumed in flood

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Saturn is the ringed sixth planet
ate means consumed, as food

explanation.surface: A planet largely swallowed up by a deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench or soak something completely is to flood it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bribe covering demand for seafood

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or bribe
a call is a demand, as in a call for action

explanation.surface: A backhander hiding a request for something from the fish counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bivalve shellfish with a fan-shaped shell, eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Prayers of star embracing nurse

indicators.note: embracing means holding round, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A celebrity hugging a nurse, offered as a devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic devotion of prayers said over nine days, so a set of prayers.

clue.text: Stay away from salt dye

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman
a stain is a dye or colouring

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid salt and food colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' looks like the seasoning, but here it means a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain or keep away from something, especially a vote or drink, is a synonymous verb.

clue.text: Hide mark from shabby stuff as well

parts.note: tat is cheap, shabby goods
too means as well, also

explanation.surface: A blemish on leather traced back to poor-quality goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, conceal; here it is skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ink design on skin is a permanent mark on one's hide, a witty way to describe it.

clue.text: Range of a record signing, initially

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The scope of a record contract, at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the great mountain range of central Europe, so a range.

clue.text: Frank returns carrying material for board covers

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other
returns means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to frank a letter is to stamp it
lace is a delicate fabric

explanation.surface: Frank comes back carrying fabric to cover a board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the verb, to stamp a letter; 'board' is the old sense of a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Small mats laid at each setting protect the table, and board is an old word for table.

clue.text: Commercial on independent group of countries is so long

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
the EU is the European Union

explanation.surface: An advert for an independent bloc of nations is very long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a comment on the advert's length; it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A French farewell used in English, equivalent to goodbye or so long.

clue.text: Waste time penning instruction to printer

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the answer sits inside the words of the phrase before it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the start of the next

explanation.surface: Someone wastes time writing directions for a printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'let it stand', a proofreader's mark telling the typesetter to ignore a correction.

clue.text: Country doctor too — he's Liberal, for a start

indicators.note: for a start takes the first letter of the word
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rural GP, and a Liberal one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like part of the phrase 'Country doctor', but it is the verb signalling the rearrangement; the Liberal's first letter leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a landlocked kingdom in southern Africa, a country.

clue.text: The French — after unusually quiet drink

indicators.note: unusually suggests an odd arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: la is the feminine form of the in French

explanation.surface: The French come after a strangely silent drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' means the French word for 'the', here the feminine form.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican spirit distilled from agave, a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Decisive stage when investments become unprofitable?

definitions.meaning: the moment after which a course of action cannot be reversed
read literally, the moment at which money put in stops yielding any return

explanation.surface: A financial adviser pinpoints the crucial moment when investments go sour.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the irreversible stage of a decision; literally it is where no return is earned.
